concepts.name: Linear algebra
concepts.summary: Vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and least squares. Nearly every model in robotics is written in this language.

concepts.name: Probability & Gaussians
concepts.summary: Random variables, Bayes' rule, and the multivariate Gaussian. The book reviews these at the start of the estimation part, and they underpin every filter that follows.

concepts.name: Calculus & ODEs
concepts.summary: Derivatives, Jacobians, and ordinary differential equations, used to describe how state changes over time.

concepts.name: Numerical optimization
concepts.summary: Minimizing a cost subject to constraints: gradients, optimality conditions, and the solvers that trajectory optimization and calibration run on.

concepts.name: Neural networks & training
concepts.summary: Layers, losses, backpropagation, and stochastic gradient descent. Needed for learned perception and learned policies.

concepts.name: Autonomy software stack
concepts.summary: The Python tooling and the idea of a modular stack where perception, estimation, planning, and control run as connected components.

concepts.name: State-space models
concepts.summary: Describe a robot by a state vector and inputs, with dynamics giving the state's rate of change. Every later control and estimation method starts here.

concepts.name: Kinematic vs. dynamic models
concepts.summary: Kinematic models relate velocities to motion and ignore forces; dynamic models include mass, inertia, and actuation. Choosing the right fidelity is a design decision.

concepts.name: Nonholonomic wheeled robots
concepts.summary: Wheels that cannot slide sideways constrain velocity but not position. The unicycle and differential-drive models capture this and recur through the book.

concepts.name: Numerical integration & simulation
concepts.summary: Step continuous dynamics forward in time with Euler or Runge–Kutta schemes, and understand when discretization error matters.

concepts.name: Optimal control problems
concepts.summary: Pose motion as choosing inputs that minimize a cost while respecting dynamics and constraints, producing an open-loop plan.

concepts.name: Indirect methods & Pontryagin
concepts.summary: Derive necessary conditions for optimality first, then solve them. This turns trajectory optimization into a boundary value problem.

concepts.name: Direct methods & transcription
concepts.summary: Discretize the trajectory and hand the whole problem to a nonlinear solver. The workhorse of practical trajectory optimization.

concepts.name: Differential flatness
concepts.summary: For some systems, all states and inputs follow from a few flat outputs and their derivatives, so smooth trajectories can be designed in those outputs directly.

concepts.name: PID control
concepts.summary: Feedback from the error, its integral, and its derivative. Simple, ubiquitous, and the baseline every other controller is compared against.

concepts.name: Linearization
concepts.summary: Approximate nonlinear dynamics near a point or trajectory with a linear model so linear tools apply. Automatic differentiation makes the Jacobians cheap.

concepts.name: LQR
concepts.summary: For linear dynamics and quadratic cost, the optimal feedback is a fixed gain matrix from a Riccati equation. The default controller for stabilizing a robot near a setpoint.

concepts.name: Trajectory tracking
concepts.summary: Close the loop around a planned trajectory so the robot follows it despite disturbances and model error.

concepts.name: iLQR & DDP
concepts.summary: Repeatedly linearize about the current trajectory and solve an LQR problem, extending LQR to nonlinear systems.

concepts.name: Model predictive control
concepts.summary: Re-solve a short-horizon trajectory optimization at every step and apply only the first input. Handles constraints explicitly.

concepts.name: Configuration space
concepts.summary: Represent every possible robot pose as a point, with obstacles becoming forbidden regions. Planning becomes finding a path between points.

concepts.name: Graph search & A*
concepts.summary: Discretize the space into a grid or graph and search it with label-correcting algorithms such as A*, using a heuristic to explore toward the goal first.

concepts.name: Sampling-based planning (PRM, RRT)
concepts.summary: Sample random configurations and connect them into a roadmap or tree. Scales to high-dimensional spaces where grids fail.

concepts.name: Potential field methods
concepts.summary: Attract the robot to the goal and repel it from obstacles with an artificial field. Fast and reactive, but prone to local minima.

concepts.name: Planning with dynamics
concepts.summary: Plan paths that respect the robot's dynamics, not just its geometry, so the result is something the robot can actually execute.

concepts.name: Robot sensors
concepts.summary: Encoders, IMUs, GPS, lidar, radar, and cameras: what each measures, at what rate, and how it fails.

concepts.name: Measurement noise models
concepts.summary: Describe sensor error statistically, usually as bias plus Gaussian noise, so estimators can weigh each reading correctly.

concepts.name: Pinhole camera model
concepts.summary: Project 3D points onto an image plane with homogeneous coordinates. The geometric basis for everything a camera tells a robot.

concepts.name: Intrinsics, extrinsics & calibration
concepts.summary: Estimate a camera's focal length, distortion, and pose relative to the robot from images of a known pattern.

concepts.name: Feature detection & matching
concepts.summary: Find distinctive image points and describe them so the same point can be matched across views, as SIFT does.

concepts.name: Epipolar geometry
concepts.summary: Two views of a scene constrain where a point in one image can appear in the other, captured by the essential and fundamental matrices.

concepts.name: Stereo depth & triangulation
concepts.summary: Recover depth from disparity between two calibrated cameras.

concepts.name: Structure from motion
concepts.summary: Jointly recover camera motion and 3D structure from many images, refined with bundle adjustment.

concepts.name: Visual odometry & loop closure
concepts.summary: Estimate the camera's motion frame to frame, and recognize revisited places to correct the drift that accumulates.

concepts.name: Image filtering & convolution
concepts.summary: Slide small kernels over an image to smooth it, find edges, or match templates. The same operation later becomes the core of CNNs.

concepts.name: Point cloud registration (ICP)
concepts.summary: Align two 3D scans by alternating between matching nearest points and solving for the best rigid transform.

concepts.name: Classical visual recognition
concepts.summary: Recognize objects from hand-designed features and classifiers, the approach learned models later replaced.

concepts.name: Convolutional neural networks
concepts.summary: Stack learned convolution filters so the network discovers its own features from data.

concepts.name: Attention & vision transformers
concepts.summary: Models that relate every part of the input to every other part through attention, now common for images, point clouds, and multimodal input.

concepts.name: Point cloud & voxel networks
concepts.summary: Architectures such as PointNet and 3D convolutions that consume lidar and depth data directly instead of images.

concepts.name: Object detection & recognition
concepts.summary: Locate and label objects with bounding boxes, the input most downstream tracking and planning modules consume.

concepts.name: 3D object detection
concepts.summary: Predict oriented 3D boxes from point clouds or voxels, which is what a planner needs to reason about other agents.

concepts.name: Semantic & instance segmentation
concepts.summary: Label every pixel or point by class, and separate individual objects of the same class.

concepts.name: Recursive Bayes filter
concepts.summary: Maintain a belief over state with two alternating steps: predict with the motion model, correct with the measurement.

concepts.name: Discrete (histogram) filter
concepts.summary: Run the Bayes filter over a grid of possible states. Exact but limited to small spaces.

concepts.name: Kalman filter
concepts.summary: The Bayes filter in closed form when dynamics are linear and noise is Gaussian.

concepts.name: EKF & UKF
concepts.summary: Extend the Kalman filter to nonlinear systems, by linearizing (EKF) or by propagating sigma points (UKF).

concepts.name: Particle filter
concepts.summary: Represent the belief with weighted samples, which handles multimodal and non-Gaussian distributions.

concepts.name: Probabilistic motion & sensor models
concepts.summary: Odometry and range-bearing models written as probability distributions, ready to plug into a filter.

concepts.name: EKF localization
concepts.summary: Estimate the robot's pose in a known map by fusing odometry with landmark measurements.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo localization
concepts.summary: Particle-filter localization that can recover from being lost or placed at an unknown starting pose.

concepts.name: EKF SLAM
concepts.summary: Add landmark positions to the state so the robot estimates its pose and the map together.

concepts.name: SLAM front end
concepts.summary: The perception side of SLAM: extract features, associate them with landmarks, reject outliers, and detect loop closures before any estimation runs.

concepts.name: Graph & factor-graph SLAM
concepts.summary: Treat poses as graph nodes and measurements as constraints, then solve for the configuration that best satisfies them all. Standard in modern SLAM.

concepts.name: Multi-sensor fusion
concepts.summary: Combine sensors with different rates and error profiles, such as IMU with GPS, into one consistent estimate.

concepts.name: Object tracking & data association
concepts.summary: Follow detected objects over time, deciding which new detection belongs to which existing track.

concepts.name: Learned fusion (BEV & features)
concepts.summary: Fuse sensors inside a network, for example in a bird's-eye-view feature space, then hand the result to classical filters. Where the classical and learned halves of the stack meet.

concepts.name: Finite state machines
concepts.summary: Hand-designed modes and transitions that sequence behaviors. Still how many deployed robots decide what to do next.

concepts.name: Markov decision processes
concepts.summary: States, actions, transition probabilities, and rewards: the formal model of sequential decisions under uncertainty.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming & Bellman
concepts.summary: Solve decisions backward in time through the principle of optimality. The same idea underlies LQR, shortest-path search, and value iteration.

concepts.name: Value & policy iteration
concepts.summary: Iterative algorithms that compute the optimal value function and policy when the model is known.

concepts.name: Reinforcement learning basics
concepts.summary: Learn to act from trial and error when the dynamics model is unknown, trading off exploration and exploitation.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo & TD learning
concepts.summary: Estimate values from sampled experience, either from full episodes or by bootstrapping from the next state's estimate.

concepts.name: Value-based RL (Q-learning)
concepts.summary: Learn action values from experience and act greedily on them, scaling to large problems with function approximation.

concepts.name: Policy gradients & actor-critic
concepts.summary: Optimize a parameterized policy directly by gradient ascent on expected return, with a learned critic to reduce variance.

concepts.name: Model-based RL & system ID
concepts.summary: Learn a dynamics model from data and plan or control with it, connecting learning back to the control chapters.

concepts.name: Behavior cloning
concepts.summary: Train a policy by supervised learning on expert demonstrations. Fast to set up, but errors compound once the robot drifts from what it saw.

concepts.name: Covariate shift
concepts.summary: A cloned policy makes small errors, drifts into states the expert never showed, and errors compound. Understanding this explains most imitation learning failures and the fixes for them.

concepts.name: Inverse reinforcement learning
concepts.summary: Infer the reward an expert seems to be optimizing, then learn a policy for that reward.
